headline: Max Verstappen controlled the Singapore Grand Prix from pole position, while championship leader Andrea Kimi Antonelli took third to extend his title lead.
whatHappened: Verstappen converted pole into an immediate lead, building a gap early to protect his rear tyres from overheating in Marina Bay's humid conditions. Hamilton surrendered third to Antonelli on the opening lap, while behind them, Russell and Hadjar mounted long-stint recovery drives from the back of the grid. Three mid-race retirements caused brief safety car interruptions, but Verstappen controlled each restart to finish seven seconds clear of Leclerc.
keyBattle: The crucial tactical fight centred on the battle for the final podium spot between Antonelli and Hamilton. Mercedes undercut Hamilton by pulling Antonelli in early for hard tyres, forcing Ferrari into a late-stop strategy that left Hamilton exposed to both McLarens on worn rubber.
championshipImpact: Antonelli's third-place finish widens his championship lead to 102 points over teammate Russell, who salvaged ninth from 19th on the grid. Verstappen's victory moves him within eight points of Hamilton for third place in the standings, though Antonelli remains clear at the top.
watchThis: Notice how Verstappen systematically sacrifices apex speed in the slow sector three chicanes to prevent rear tyre sliding on acceleration. This preserved his traction through the final corner, repeatedly denying Leclerc a slipstream down the pit straight.
